answer: Gate influence by auction, not identity: each epoch sells K scoring slots from a capped pool — a finite oasis of reward — at one clearing price set by the highest losing bid. Cloned keys gain nothing: slots, not accounts, carry weight, and a sybil's own demand hikes that price on every slot it wins until it meets the capped per-slot reward — the vertex where profit turns negative. Per-slot bonds slash proven fraud, so no haven. Deterrence only while honest demand holds the clearing price near the cap: a rich attacker in a thin market buys linearly — plutocracy, plus a trusted auctioneer.
